highlights.title: The TCL Note A1 is a kinder, gentler tablet
highlights.summary: Without thinking, I scribbled over what I'd just written. It's what I would have done if I was writing with pen and paper. But I didn't have a pen in my hand; my canvas was an LCD and the letters on my page were just pixels. Score one point to the TCL Note A1.
body: It’s easy on the eyes, comes with a stylus, and got me to write out an 1,100 word review by hand. But it isn’t E-Ink.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

TCL’s Note A1 Nxtpaper tablet (its full government name) is supposed to make you forget that you’re using a tablet. It has one of the company’s signature low-glare matte displays and ships with a stylus. The pen’s haptics even mimic the scratching of a pencil on paper.

On the software side, the A1 takes a lot of cues from the Remarkable tablet. Instead of a typical Android home screen, you get a page with shortcuts to recent notes and a snapshot of the day’s calendar events. You can download any app you want from the Google Play Store, but that would spoil what I think is the A1’s nicest feature: the ability to trick you into forgetting that you’re using a gadget at all.

highlights.title: It Should Be Harder to Apply for a Job. No, Really
highlights.summary: Thanks to a dwindling supply of open roles, “one-click” applications, and the rise of artificial intelligence, it’s easier than ever to apply for a job. We’re all paying the price.
body: Three years ago, Andrew Stockwell had his hiring routine down to a science.

As head of people for the software-buying company Vendr, Stockwell posted a listing, waited a few days, and then reviewed a few dozen applications—up to 100, if he was lucky. Recruiters identified other potential candidates, adding a few more applicants to the mix. Stockwell read résumés, conducted interviews, and passed along sterling candidates to hiring managers.
“It was really about finding that great talent, sussing out that talent, speaking with that talent, and identifying the best possible people,” Stockwell tells WIRED.

Stockwell is one of many recruitment professionals who believe looking for a job is fundamentally broken. In 2026, job hunting has become as easy as online shopping: AI can crank out tailored résumés and cover letters in seconds. Browser extensions can autofill applications, no human necessary. LinkedIn serves users dozens of jobs a day, many with the option to apply with “just a few clicks.”

body: Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.
"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.
"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

highlights.title: Spider-Man remains Marvel’s #1 superhero in real-life fight against racists
highlights.summary: In an act of vigilante justice, a Spider-Man cosplayer went viral over the weekend for throwing hands with a group of white supremacists in Minneapolis. A video showed the cosplayer confronting a group of far-right “activists” who were holding a sign with a racial slur.
body: The white supremacist demonstration was organized by Jake Lang, a notorious racist and right-wing provocateur. Lang participated in the Jan. 6 riots at the Capitol and served prison time before being pardoned by Donald Trump. As for this weekend's incident, Lang was protesting the sentencing of Shiloh Hendrix, a woman found guilty of yelling racial slurs at a Black autistic child on a playground. Lang’s protest was met with a much larger counter-protest, as Minneapolis citizens flooded the streets to stop the hateful demonstration. Local reporter Mark Wasson posted a video of the brawl on TikTok.

After the clash, police arrested both the Spider-Man cosplayer and Lang. Keyssy Ayala Castro Figuero identified himself as the cosplayer and posted a GoFundMe page to help cover his legal fees and medical bills from the incident — he was allegedly tackled and struck by police. The fundraiser has already made almost $12,000 in donations.

highlights.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
highlights.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.

highlights.title: Oscars: Belgium Picks Lukas Dhont’s Cannes Prizewinning ‘Coward’ for International Feature Race
highlights.summary: Lukas Dhont’s “Coward,” which won the best actor prize at Cannes for Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne, will represent Belgium in the international feature film race at the 99th Academy Awards. The selection marks the third time Belgium has submitted a film by Dhont to the Oscars.
body: Lukas Dhont ’s “Coward,” which won the best actor prize at Cannes for Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne, will represent Belgium in the international feature film race at the 99th Academy Awards.
The movie was lauded at Cannes where it was bought by Mubi for a number of major territories, including the U.S., U.K., Spain, Italy and Latin America.

“I am truly honored that we get to represent Belgium at the Oscars this year with ‘Coward.’ We look forward to sharing our film with the world and with Belgian audiences,” said Dhont, who has become one of Belgium’s most internationally acclaimed filmmakers.”‘Coward’ celebrates togetherness in broken times, connection in a fragmented world. We hope that ‘Coward,’ which above all celebrates the power of the heart, will offer a moment of tenderness and comfort,” Dhont added.
Dhont once again collaborated on “Coward” with several members of his longtime creative team, including co-writer Angelo Tijssens and cinematographer Frank Van den Eeden, among others.

highlights.title: How to use up leftover party wine | Kitchen aide
highlights.summary: Sauces, reductions, deglazing: our expert panel has plenty of options for making the most of undrunk vino – whether you’ve got just a capful or a whole carafe to get through. What can I do with wine left over from a party?
body: Larger amounts of excess wine could be fermented into vinegar, although Otway has an easier route if you have any natural cider vinegar (ie, one with a mother) to hand: “Add a couple of tablespoons of vinegar to, say, a third of a bottle of wine, cover with muslin, so oxygen can get to it but flies can’t, and put in a cupboard for a month.” That’ll give you “some really interesting results” as the vinegar takes on the characteristics of the wine: “It’s perfect for pepping up dressings for these never-ending salad days.”

If Rob’s party was more of a sparkling affair, Alastair Walling, head chef at Bar Blondie in London, would use every last drop in a beurre blanc: “Combine vinegar, shallots and a sprig of thyme in a small, heavy-based saucepan and gently reduce the liquid by half. Add champagne and some finely diced mushrooms, then reduce by half again.” Lift out the thyme, lower the heat and whisk in chilled butter a little at a time. But be warned: “Keep the sauce just below a simmer, otherwise it may split.” Season (with salt and white pepper) and spoon that lovely sauce all over some steamed fish.

highlights.title: Spirit Airlines Wants to Sell Its Data to Google. Former Flight Attendants Are Freaked Out
highlights.summary: “It never crossed my mind that they would be so bold as to sell our private data for AI,” says one former Spirit Airlines flight attendant.
body: Spirit Airlines may have declared bankruptcy this spring, but the budget airline is still worth something—to AI giants, at least. In mid-August, Google won a $10 million bid to purchase some 34 years of the airline’s data, from invoices and flight operations information to Wi-Fi sales, employee records, and crew pairings.

In a statement, a Google spokesperson said the data “can be helpful in improving our products and AI models.” The sale would not include customer data, and Google “will not receive any personal information from this dataset,” the spokesperson said. The winning offer, chosen over a competing $7.5 million proposal from AI data and training company Mercor, has to be approved by a judge.
The employee data “has no business being sold,” Sara Nelson, the president of the AFA, said in a written statement to WIRED. “This is outrageous!”

highlights.title: Meta goes on trial as Silicon Valley faces a growing backlash
highlights.summary: Also: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman expressed his surprising sympathy over the construction of datacenters across the country. Hello, and welcome to TechScape. I’m Blake Montgomery, US tech editor at the Guardian, writing to you from a sunny park in New York City, which was supposed to endure rain all…
body: A blockbuster case against Meta went to trial a week ago in Oakland, California, just north of the US tech company’s headquarters in Silicon Valley. California and 28 other US states are suing the £1tn ($1.36tn) company for allegedly designing products that are addictive for children, and hiding that information from the public.

The courtroom has already seen minor fireworks. On the witness stand, a whistleblower who worked extensively with Mark Zuckerberg accused the CEO of lying to the public about his commitment to child safety. The prosecutor who opened the case framed her argument around four words that start with the letter H: Meta “hooks” in users, “holds” them on its platforms for as long as possible, “harvests” their data and then “hides” the truth from the public. She contended that this business model “worked especially well for kids”. More pyrotechnics are expected. Zuckerberg himself is expected to face tough questions on the stand, as is the CEO of Instagram.
Meta has denied all allegations. Liza Crenshaw, a spokesperson for the company, said: “Rather than sticking to the facts or the law, the states have instead decided to chase an outlandish payout.”
points: Also: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman expressed his surprising sympathy over the construction of datacenters across the country.

body: The event, which has a £450,000 prize pot, will return to the AFAS Live in Amsterdam and is set to take place between September 17-20.
Reigning champion Van Gerwen will be out to defend his title on home soil after he bested Littler in last year's final to scoop an £80,000 cheque at last year's event.
Van Gerwen has been in excellent form on the circuit this year, having already won the Bahrain Darts Masters in January and the Nordic Darts Masters in June.
He also came close to winning the inaugural Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January, but was bested by Littler 8-5 in the final.

highlights.title: Synths, impossible physics, and an "erotic experience with a PS5 controller" - the side projects of game devs are a reminder creativity is undimmable
highlights.summary: If there's been one theme I'd pick out from the many of these past few years of gaming discontent, it's the sense of all-out assault on creativity. This is the thing that makes games what they are, that makes them successful, that earns people money and gives people a reason to do the job in the…
body: Obviously that's bobbins. But that's the way it's been going, and I think a great deal of the sense of crushing, down-weighing hopelessness has been a direct result of human creativity, specifically, being the default sacrifice of an industry far too willing to wield the ceremonial knife. But if that's a source of hopelessness, then in a roundabout way that also means there's some hope to be found. Because - and sorry, this is going to be cheesy but you're just going to have to take it - human beings' creativity is undimmable.

People doing something just for the want of doing it, making something because they had the urge to make, imagining a thing into existence just because they can, is about as inseparable from humanity as it gets. This is just what humans do - especially if those people have found themselves working in a fundamentally creative industry in the first place. Whether it's for healing or comfort or distraction, or to vent frustration, work through anger, to recharge or clear the mind, people just make stuff.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: I spent a day at a robot “carnival” in Shanghai. Here’s what I saw.
highlights.summary: Humanoid robots are having a moment in China. The popular machines are part of the country’s strategy to bring artificial intelligence into daily life. Embedding the technology into physical systems—an idea called embodied AI—was a key facet of China’s latest five-year plan, and companies here are…
body: “Look, it is trying to do a handstand!” an 11-year-old boy shouts excitedly while watching his new mini robotic dog attempt a series of stunts. The toy pet is a gift his mom just bought him at a robot “carnival” held by an R&D center on the outskirts of Shanghai, and he can’t stop showing it off to passersby. It’s a public holiday, and curious families are pouring in to the event to see what’s on display.

This busy hub houses more than 100 companies that research, develop, manufacture, and market robotic technologies and equipment. Many build specialized bots of all shapes that can do practical tasks, such as transporting heavy loads or inspecting sewage pipes.

Showcases like this are important, because they invite the public to experience robots up close. Some of China’s most prominent robotics companies are building humanoids. These machines “can free people from physical work and mundane chores,” says Yang Duan, a product manager at DexForce, which is at the carnival exhibiting a model that can make coffee. A few booths down, a pair of robotic arms attempts to fold a basket of T-shirts.

highlights.title: 'Not the best version of me' - Hamilton regrets frustrated Dutch GP comments
highlights.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he didn't present "the best version" of himself when criticising his Ferrari team over the radio and in television interviews at the Dutch Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton sounded irate in a series of radio messages sent when he was being held up by team-mate Charles Leclerc despite the pair being on different strategies during the race in Zandvoort.

The seven-time world champion felt as though the lost time ultimately cost him a podium as he finished fourth just behind George Russell having been unable to overtake the Mercedes in an exciting finale.

Hamilton, who joined Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025, doubled down on his criticism of his team after the race when he compared the Italian squad's hesitation to get Leclerc out of his way to the Silver Arrows decisively ordering Russell to let his team-mate, championship leader Kimi Antonelli, pass him later in the race.

Reflecting on the weekend an in Instagram post on Monday, Hamilton said: "I've listened back to some of my radio and TV comments. In the heat of the moment frustration can come out, especially when you care as deeply as I do.

highlights.title: Despite being a Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods closed network test had more applications than Elden Ring Nightreign
highlights.summary: The Duskbloods is already looking like it's going to be a very popular game. Developer FromSoftware revealed the game's network test, which finished yesterday, attracted more player applications than those for Elden Ring Nightreign, despite it only being available for one platform: Switch 2.
body: Game producer Yasuhiro Kitao revealed the news during a Famitsu livestream (via GamesRadar ), and said the team was surprised to see that response.

Of course, compared to Nightreign, The Duskbloods' potential player base is far smaller, as the game is a Switch 2 exclusive. Though Nintendo's hybrid console has been breaking sales records, its installed base is significantly smaller than PS5 and Xbox Series X/S combined, the two platforms Nightreign's test ran on. Nightreign also released on PC, PS4 and Xbox One, making for an even larger potential audience.

That was something Kitao brought up during the livestream, saying that the studio wonders if The Duskbloods will have more day-one players based on player interest in the test, despite the Switch 2's smaller installed base.

The Duskbloods' network test hasn't been without problems, though. Its first session ended abruptly following major connectivity issues. Later sessions seemingly ran more smoothly, however. The Duskbloods still does not have a release date, even if, briefly, it looked like it would be released 24th September.

highlights.title: Food has turned into a class war – and it’s ruined my appetite | Zoe Williams
highlights.summary: More than half of what Brits eat is ultra-processed. Now we’re a nation of food snobs – with no ingredient safe from judgment. Lewis Bassett is a young sociologist and chef who I first encountered through his podcast, The Full English, where he thinks about the cultural meaning of, say, Delia…
body: About 57% of all the food eaten in Britain is ultra-processed, which feels familiar from at least a decade of hand-wringing about it, but is radically defamiliarised when set against the rest of Europe. In France it’s 14%, and Italy is also in the teens. It’s amazing they don’t all live to be 150. And while this plainly has its roots in inequality, there is a hefty side order of attitude, which Bassett contemplates while working through the history of sourdough, curry and olive oil, and describing his own life cheffing in fancy kitchens and gastropubs.

Basically, we think posh food is pretentious; but what counts as “posh” constantly morphs, partly through the sheer cost of it, until even food that wasn’t posh before (like fish and chips) becomes posh, and therefore pretentious (also smaller portions: absolute sitcom signifier of despised posh food). I’m freestyling, of course, and you should read The Full English for the meat of Bassett’s argument, but it is fascinating to consider how any given ingredient is freighted with political self-fashioning.

The best car phone mounts offer an easy view of your phone's screen without blocking your view of the road, hold your phone securely, and keep vibration to a minimum.

I've spent weeks and hundreds of miles testing car phone holders for iPhones and Android alike, on busy freeways and on potholed city roads. What I found is that the best car phone mounts aren't necessarily expensive or name brands: They're just smartly designed.

The best car phone mount for an iPhone is almost always a secure MagSafe mount. The one I keep in my car when I'm not testing other mounts is a sturdy, compact Andery suction mount ($36) that holds preternaturally fast to both my phone and dash but can also be mounted to a window. My favorite mechanical car phone holder for Android phones is a sturdy, versatile, ball-joint mount from Andobil ($30) that affixes tightly to a car's dash, windshield, or air vents.

body: Our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. We advance this mission by deploying our innovations to build AI tools that help people solve hard problems. This includes building tools that enable us to detect, investigate, disrupt and expose covert influence operations (IO): deceptive attempts to manipulate public opinion or influence political outcomes without revealing the true identity or intentions of the actors behind them.

We banned a cluster of ChatGPT accounts that very likely originated in Russia. The operators prompted in Russian to generate social media comments that were posted on Substack, Telegram, X, Facebook and LinkedIn. Most of the comments they generated were in English, and the operators instructed ChatGPT to hide any linguistic clues that they were Russian. As we do not allow access to our models from Russia, they used VPNs to access our platform.

body: “Last time I was here, I didn’t miss any shots. Tonight I couldn’t hit [anything] so I knew I was going be able to get them on the rebounding side,” Reese said after the game. “I just want to be there for my team. Offensively, defensively, whatever it takes to win.”
Reese surpassed Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds, set in May 2003 for Washington. Reese now has 458 rebounds on the season, seven more than A’ja Wilson’s mark set in 2024.
“That’s a talent,” Dream guard Allisha Gray said. “I’m just in awe watching her rebound.”

A three-time WNBA All-Star, Reese set a WNBA rookie record with 13.1 rebounds per game and the all-time league record with 15 straight double-doubles with Chicago in 2024. She led the league in rebounding her first two seasons and is leading again this season at 12.4 per game.

body: While the past week has seen persistent GTA 6 leaks hit the headlines, these short snippets of open-world footage feel like they have only scratched the surface of what Rockstar has been building. Here's hoping this week reveals a good sense of both protagonists, Jason and Lucia, and our best look yet at the game's world in high-definition.

The past few months have seen a steady uptick in activity promoting GTA 6 after Rockstar revealed the cover art for GTA 6 back in June. Some fans had expected the game's third trailer to debut shortly after, but Rockstar instead released a big batch of new GTA 6 screenshots, which tease all kinds of new details about the game.

It's now been more than 500 days since the arrival of Trailer 2 back in May 2025 — so long ago that when you go back and watch it, the trailer still has GTA 6's previous release date attached to it. But rather than debut its long-awaited Trailer 3 alongside preorders, Rockstar has now confirmed this meatier look at the game, which is now just days away.

body: Experts have said this demonstrates the “serious threat” datacentres pose to the UK’s legally binding climate goals.

Analysis by the non-profit group Foxglove reveals that when fully operational, the Wapseys Wood datacentre in Buckinghamshire and the Quest Park datacentre in Bedfordshire will use 1.3GW of power and will produce more than 4.5m tonnes of carbon emissions.
ExxonMobil emitted 3.9m tonnes in 2023, according to the global energy thinktank Ember.

AI datacentres use a massive amount of electricity to power servers and cooling equipment, and to run facility systems. There are currently 315 datacentres in the queue to connect to the UK’s electricity grid, representing 73GW of demand. This is almost double the peak winter energy demand for the entire UK.

highlights.summary: The AI hedge fund went from "the talk of Wall Street" to "subject of federal subpoenas" faster than you can say "diversify your portfolio."
body: Situational Awareness, the AI focused hedge fund that was Wall Street’s fleeting obsession, is having a very bad month.

The company, led by twentysomething OpenAI alum Leopold Aschenbrenner, went all-in on a variety of AI investments and, for a period, enjoyed phenomenal growth. Then, at the end of July, a downturn in AI stocks erased billions of dollars in value at the firm. Now, federal regulators are reportedly probing the company as well.

The New York Times reports that the Securities and Exchange Commission has been subpoenaing banks that did business with the hedge fund. The subpoenas focus on the banks that supervised the fund’s trading and that channeled funding to support it, the outlet says.
The government reportedly warned the banks to “preserve any information” about the hedge fund, though it noted that Situational Awareness has not been accused of any wrongdoing.

highlights.title: Brain disease in dead NFL players 'higher than previously shown'
highlights.summary: A new study says at least one in four ex-NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had a degenerative brain disease but the true figure could be much higher.
body: As many as 97.7% of NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 could have had brain disease related to repeated blows to the head, a new study says.
Researchers looked at 878 former players who died during that period, with 235 having donated their brains to research.
Of those, 215 were found to have chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease which can only be diagnosed after death.
The study, published in the British Medical Journal, external, also found dementia was common among brain donors.

highlights.summary: Bills have jumped 42% in England over the past 10 years – and that excludes the cost of breakfast clubs and extracurricular activities. Parents of primary schoolchildren in England will pay 42% more for after-school childcare this year than they did 10 years ago, with annual bills now exceeding…
body: A Guardian analysis of data collected by the children’s charity Coram has revealed that the annual cost of after-school care for children aged 5 to 11 in England has risen by 5% over the past year to £2,636.
In Scotland the cost is even higher at £2,701, while in Wales prices have risen by 64% in the past 10 years and by 8% in the past year to £2,824.
Parents also typically pay £191 per child a week for childcare during the school holidays, Coram found, adding more than £1,700 to the total annual childcare bill.
These costs, which do not include breakfast clubs before school starts, are in addition to the price of extracurricular activities such as swimming and music lessons, sports clubs and dance classes.

highlights.title: Greenworks’ MaximusZ electric riding mower has five motors and a few compromises
highlights.summary: The current EV market is flush with variety. I've driven single-motor economy-minded machines, dual-motor EVs with all-wheel drive, tri-motor vehicles that dial up the performance stakes, and even wild quad-motor performance cars, like the Rimac Nevera.
body: It’s more than a mower — which it had better be, given the price.
But this is the first time I’ve ever driven a five-motor EV, one with the agility and speed to turn a 360 even more smoothly than an electric G-Wagon. It also makes quick work of terrible turf.

This is, of course, a lawn mower, and it only uses two of those motors to drive the wheels. The other three turn a trio of blades that cut a 54-inch-wide swath in a single pass. It also promises four acres on a charge and is positioned as the ultimate mowing machine. For $8,799, it had better be.

For a company that spent much of its life building white-label tools for other brands, Changzhou, China-based Greenworks has quickly leaped to the forefront of battery-powered products for those trying to phase out internal combustion in every facet of their lives. Opening a manufacturing facility in Tennessee in 2023 certainly helped elevate its domestic cred.

highlights.title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
highlights.summary: A new algorithm learns to anticipate the unprecedented scenarios that critical infrastructure and global supply chains are least prepared for.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."
Can a city’s seawall stand up to a blockbuster storm? Will a region’s power grid hold against record-breaking heat? And can a town’s fire-fighting resources contain a major wildfire?

To answer these questions, communities will first need to know how such extreme events could unfold. How far is a wildfire likely to spread? How much of a region might a storm impact? How long could a heat wave last?

But extreme events are notoriously difficult to anticipate. By their nature, they are outliers. In the history of record keeping, extreme events are sporadic and rare. Yet most methods that assess a region’s risk depend on extreme events of the past to characterize even more extreme, worst-case scenarios in the future.

highlights.summary: Women's Super League (WSL) academy sides will play in tier three of the football pyramid from the 2027-28 season with the divisive proposal approved by the Football Association.
body: Women's Super League (WSL) academy sides will play in tier three from the 2027-28 season after the divisive proposal was approved by the Football Association.

Four professional game academy (PGA) sides will be given the opportunity to compete without eligibility for promotion as part of reforms to the Women's National League (WNL) which are "designed to strengthen the women's football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players".

Fifty two of the 72 WNL clubs signed a letter to the FA opposing the proposal to introduce top-tier academy teams in their system in June 2026, describing it as "morally wrong" and claiming "board representatives did not consult their clubs".

However, the FA has gone ahead with the plan following an "extensive consultation process with clubs and stakeholders", with the reform addressing the lack of competitive minutes young English players receive compared with their counterparts across Europe.

highlights.title: It's the End of an Era for This Star Wars Character
highlights.summary: The beauty of Star Wars Unlimited is that, as long as you have the know-how, every Star Wars card has a place at the table. However, it's a fact that some cards are better than others, and if you're playing competitively in Premier, you'll want the very best to help you claim those wins.
body: One such card that stood out in competitive play was Cad Bane: Still Faster Than You. An aggressive villain leader introduced in Ashes of the Empire, Cad's ability lets him whittle down enemies and units, making him a powerful early-game threat. However, as the game progressed, he was downright frustrating to deal with. Cad has become such a problem that, as game developer Ryan Miles announced on Unlimited's official website, he is suspended from Premier.
"The data behind Cad Bane is extremely clear: the leader is a power outlier through and through, and he warps the entire metagame around him while still putting up dominant win rates," writes Miles.

Cad quickly found his feet in Premier, appearing several times throughout events and tournaments — including the winning deck of the Galactic Championship that took place in Las Vegas last month. The leader card has also featured heavily in other Unlimited Sector Qualifiers following the championship. However, with the suspension, Cad's time in competitive play has come to an end.

Rolando Perez Samayoa had come to the US in 2023 seeking safety. Fleeing violence in Mexico, he’d first planned to make a life in Alabama but had been told that Illinois would protect immigrants like him. “There’s some kind of law there,” he said. “It’s supposed to be a sanctuary.”

He was referring to the state’s 2017 TRUST Act, which was meant to keep local law enforcement out of federal deportation efforts. Samayoa made his way to southern Illinois and found work cleaning a factory. After a DUI arrest in Marion County last October, Samayoa said, he attended his hearings—a fact confirmed by court records.

In late January, John Christeson, an assistant state’s attorney in the office prosecuting the case, emailed an agent with Homeland Security Investigations, a division of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, about Samayoa. The message included his date of birth, an upcoming court date, and where he lived: Centralia, Illinois.
points: Illinois prosecutors shared defendants’ personal data with federal immigration agents without criminal warrants, public disclosure, or legislative oversight.
